title: Lakshya Sen beats Tanaka to reach Kumamoto Masters semi-finals; Srikanth loses
dek: Sen is now the only Indian left at the Super 500 event in Japan, where he is chasing points for the World Tour Finals.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Lakshya Sen reached the semi-finals of the Kumamoto Masters Japan, a BWF Super 500 tournament, on Friday with a 21-16, 21-15 win over Japan's Yushi Tanaka in 40 minutes. It was Sen's third win in three meetings with Tanaka.

Kidambi Srikanth, who had beaten Japan's fifth seed Kodai Naraoka on Thursday, lost his quarter-final 22-24, 15-21 to Japan's Koki Watanabe. It was Watanabe's first win over the former world No. 1 in three meetings. Sen, the eighth seed and world No. 13, is now the only Indian left in the tournament.

He plays Indonesia's Alwi Farhan in the semi-finals on Saturday. The final is on Sunday, 15 November.

Sen arrived in Japan after winning the Hylo Open in Germany earlier this month. The result matters for his season: he needs to finish in the top eight of the World Tour standings to qualify for the BWF World Tour Finals in December, and was 10th in the race at the start of the week, according to the standings reported then.
